methodSelector.label: Method
methodSelector.combinableHint: Pick one or more methods to include in your weighted synthesis.
methodSelector.exclusivityHint: SDE and EV/EBITDA cannot be combined. Omzet and the English revenue key count as one method.
methodSelector.arrMultipleDescription: ARR lens for SaaS. Business model and type control which SaaS metrics are shown.
methodSelector.dcfDescription: Key rates, live FCFF preview, and smart defaults from history and accounting import—defensible DCF in minutes, not days.
methodSelector.adjustedNavDescription: Net asset value after revaluing assets and liabilities to market or fair value. Combine with multiples or DCF in weighted synthesis.
methodSelector.sdeMultipleDescription: For micro-SMEs and sole proprietorships (revenue < €5M). Adds owner salary back to EBITDA.
methodSelector.fiscal4xDescription: Belgian fiscal reference formula. Use for internal transfers and succession planning—not arm's-length M&A.
methodSelector.fiscalDisclaimerText: For internal transfers, succession planning, or tax rulings only. Not intended for external M&A transactions.
methodSelector.revenueDriverText: For this method, top-line revenue is the main anchor. EBITDA normalizations remain available, but only as secondary context here.
methodSelector.sdeExplainer: SDE (Seller's Discretionary Earnings) adds the owner's salary back to EBITDA. This reflects the true cash flow available to a buyer who replaces the owner. Enter the total annual owner compensation below.

sections.dcfDiscountAndTerminalAria: Weighted average cost of capital and terminal value
sections.discountTerminalLead: After your cash flows look right, set the discount rate and terminal assumption.

methodSelector.forecastDefaultsLead: Most valuations: enter revenue growth and EBITDA margin, then check the live table below. We suggest growth, margin, WACC, and bridge drivers from your historical years and business profile, and from accounting import (CapEx/D&A) when you pull data—then refine. Advanced FCFF drivers stay on defaults unless you need to tune them.

forecastDefaultsProvenance.history: Defaults from your history & profile (sector WACC band)
forecastDefaultsProvenance.both: History + profile + import CapEx/D&A (same pipeline as bulk valuation)

methodSelector.forecastDefaultsEditableHint: Suggested % are editable—change any field to match your judgment.
methodSelector.advancedDriversHelp: Most accountants can leave these on sector defaults and only adjust them when a specific case needs it.
methodSelector.fcffOnlyForecastDefaultsNotice: In “Without EBITDA” mode you enter yearly FCFF in the forecast table below, so growth, margin, and bridge-driver percentages are not used here.
methodSelector.dcfCapexFootnote: CapEx is cash investments. If historical capex is missing in your data, the valuation engine may use depreciation as a maintenance-capex proxy when deriving defaults.
methodSelector.applyForecastYearsDescription: Project {count, plural, one {# forecast year} other {# forecast years}} from your percentages: revenue growth, EBITDA margin, CapEx, D&A, ΔNWC, and tax—then compute FCFF for each year.
methodSelector.fcffOnlyTerminalNotice: In “Without EBITDA” mode, forecast rows have no EBITDA—terminal value uses perpetual growth (Gordon), not an EBITDA exit multiple.

fieldHints.dcfNwcPct: ΔNWC is the yearly cash effect of working capital: receivables, payables, and inventory. It is modeled as a share of revenue and is subtracted in the FCFF bridge.
fieldHints.dcfWaccSummary: WACC is the blended discount rate for future cash flows: it weights the cost of equity and after-tax cost of debt. Expand the breakdown to tune inputs.

fields.sdePreviewAutoCalculated: Aligned with omni-calc (same rules as the engine)
fields.sdePreviewNeedFinancials: Enter a complete historical year (revenue + EBITDA) to preview SDE and implied EV.
fields.sdePreviewUnavailableCap: SDE is intended for revenue under €5M; preview is disabled above that cap.
fields.sdePreviewUnavailableEbitda: Omni SDE preview requires positive EBITDA from your latest complete year.
fields.sdePreviewFootnote: Enterprise value here is SDE × multiple only. Net debt, adjustments, and synthesis are applied in the full valuation.
fields.revenueQualityPreviewFootnote: Ratios from your latest complete year + inputs; EV multiples are calibration-backed server-side.
fields.navPreviewFootnote: Sum of adjustments entered; full NAV is computed in the engine.
fields.fiscalPreviewFootnote: 4× EBITDA anchor matches Belgian fiscal reference; ownership multiplier may differ in the full run.
fields.fiscalPreviewOwnershipStakeHint: Matches omni: (book + anchor) × (shares for sale ÷ 100). Manual flow keeps 100% stake unless the product exposes partial stakes later.
fields.fiscalPreviewUnavailableNonBe: Fiscal reference applies to Belgian companies (company country).
fields.fiscalPreviewUnavailableEbitda: Positive EBITDA is required for the 4× anchor.
fields.fiscalPreviewUnavailableMissingEbitda: Add a complete historical year with EBITDA to preview the fiscal anchor.
fields.fiscalPreviewUnavailableMissingEquity: Book equity is missing from the latest year row — anchor is shown; full fiscal equity needs balance-sheet equity (or assets − liabilities).

methodSelector.realEstateCarveOutHint: Use this when the buyer acquires the operating company but rents the property from the seller after closing. The engine removes the property value from the deal and deducts market rent from the EBITDA basis.
methodSelector.estimatedMarketRentEbitdaHint: Enter your best estimate of annual market rent (not book). The valuation engine uses this to normalize EBITDA when the operating company no longer owns the bricks.
methodSelector.terminalGrowthHighWarning: Perpetual growth above long-run GDP is uncommon; auditors often question rates above 3%. Use a higher rate only if you can defend it in the file.

saasProjectionPreview.title: 5-year ARR projection
saasProjectionPreview.description: For SaaS DCF work, this preview compounds the current ARR or MRR baseline with the selected growth and retention assumptions.

saasImported.description: Pre-filled from {provider} for fiscal year {year} with {confidence}% confidence. Values are derived from recurring-looking revenue in your imported ledger—not subscription-system analytics. You can still adjust any field manually before running the valuation.

calculationBreakdown.methodologyIntro: Manufacturing companies with €1-5M revenue are typically valued at 5.0×-6.0× EBITDA. The 5.5× is based on recent transactions and accounts for:

methodDescriptions.upswitch_adaptive: Blends the strongest signals from your dossier into one defensible headline equity value.
methodDescriptions.arr_multiple: ARR × an EV/ARR-style multiple, adjusted for NRR, churn, growth, and concentration risk.
methodDescriptions.ebitda_multiple: Normalized EBITDA × a market multiple — standard for trading companies with reliable earnings.
methodDescriptions.omzet_multiple: Revenue × a multiple — useful when margins swing or peers are quoted on sales.
methodDescriptions.revenue_multiple: Revenue × a multiple (same idea as turnover / omzet multiple).
methodDescriptions.sde_multiple: Seller discretionary earnings × a multiple — common for owner-operated SMEs.
methodDescriptions.adjusted_nav: Adjusted net asset value from the balance sheet — floor or anchor for asset-heavy cases; combine with multiples/DCF in synthesis when appropriate.
methodDescriptions.fiscal_4x: Belgian fiscal reference (notional): book equity + 4× normalized EBITDA.
methodDescriptions.dcf: Discounted cash flow (DCF): projects future cash flows and discounts them to today — intrinsic value. Only selectable when the engine can compute DCF (no exclusion); otherwise the reason appears below.

preparerMultiple.title: EV/EBITDA multiple (advanced)
preparerMultiple.description: The Upswitch SME Index benchmark is your anchor—adjust only when your judgment requires it. Standardized reason tags help Upswitch refine market calibration over time while client reports stay on one clear headline.
preparerMultiple.applyHint: This control only supports the EV/EBITDA benchmark multiple. Changes apply only after you recalculate.
preparerMultiple.benchmarkHint: Based on the Upswitch SME index for this business type.
preparerMultiple.previewTemplate: A baseline industry multiple of {benchmark}x was used, derived from the Upswitch SME Index. A {adjustmentLabel} of {delta}x was applied by the preparer ({applied}x total). Justification: {reason}.
preparerMultiple.sliderHint: Anchor: benchmark median. Drag to adjust; then pick a reason and recalculate.
preparerMultiple.recalculateNeedForm: Complete the calculator form once, then use Recalculate.
preparerMultiple.extremeWarning: This multiple is far outside the typical band for this business type. Confirm to proceed.
preparerMultiple.recalcHint: Change the main form and recalculate, or use Recalculate — your adjustment is included when it differs from the benchmark and a reason is selected.
preparerMultiple.extremeServerToast: Multiple outside guardrails: confirm the checkbox and try again, or move closer to the benchmark.
preparerMultiple.hintFiscalMethod: Fiscal reference uses a fixed 4× EBITDA multiple — firm adjusted multiple does not apply to this method.
preparerMultiple.hintOtherMethod: Benchmark vs applied multiple is shown for EV/EBITDA, revenue multiple, or the Upswitch market approach. For other methods this panel is contextual only.

methodBreakdown.formulaMultiple: Normalized EBITDA x applied multiple -> enterprise value -> net debt and balance sheet adjustments -> equity value.
methodBreakdown.formulaArr: ARR × applied EV/ARR multiple → enterprise value → net debt → equity value.
methodBreakdown.formulaDcf: Discounted cash flows and terminal value combine into enterprise value, then move to equity value.
methodBreakdown.formulaFiscal: Belgian fiscal anchor: book equity + 4x normalized EBITDA.
methodBreakdown.formulaNav: Adjusted net asset value starts from the corrected balance sheet and then moves to equity value.
methodBreakdown.formulaRevenue: Revenue x applied multiple -> enterprise value -> net debt and balance sheet adjustments -> equity value.
methodBreakdown.formulaSde: Adjusted seller discretionary earnings x selected multiple -> enterprise value -> equity value.
